title: A three-dimensional typology of agency for advanced AI systems
creators: Willem Fourie
tags: Foundations & Taxonomies; Trust, Delegation & Accountability; Policy and Governance
summary: Develops a three-dimensional typology of agency for frontier AI systems along the dimensions of nature (moral or legal), mode (individual or collective) and locus (human or non-human), yielding eight instantiations classified as conventional, contested or controversial. Argues for separating legal from moral agency to allow consideration of individual, legal, non-human agency in light of instrumental goal pursuit complicating attribution of AI actions to humans.

title: Rethinking the Evaluation and Optimization of LLM-Based Social Simulation
creators: Pei Wang; Xu Chen; Ji-Rong Wen
tags: Simulation and Digital Twins; Evaluations; Datasets
summary: The paper argues that accuracy-based evaluation and hard-label training are unreliable for LLM-based social simulation because human responses are draws from a distribution. It introduces an entropy-based subjectivity coefficient, a soft-label training method (SALT) that pools outputs from semantically nearby inputs with a subjectivity-adaptive radius, and SUBJSIM, a benchmark of 19,300 contexts from 193 annotators over 100 subjective questions.

title: Inadvertent Context Leakage in Language Models
creators: Jaiden Fairoze; Neal Mangaokar; Kamalika Chaudhuri; Sanjam Garg; Saeed Mahloujifar
tags: Security & Adversarial Robustness; Emergent Harms and Capabilities; Monitoring
summary: An empirical study of whether sensitive information held in a language model's context window is recoverable from the model's ordinary, non-adversarial outputs. Using a black-box adaptive attack across eight proprietary models, the authors reconstruct 2- and 4-digit in-context secrets, report that more capable models leak more, and demonstrate a classifier inferring semantic attributes of user memories and an RL-trained adversary extracting full SSNs from a production-style agent.

title: Bringing analytic rigor to agentic AI for science: The Brain Researcher platform for neuroimaging data analysis
creators: Zijiao Chen; Nicholas Lu; Xinhui Li; Jocelyn A. Ricard; Ce Ju; Huan H. Wang; Christian Kindermann; Jeanette A. Mumford; Steven Dillmann; James Kent; Alejandro de la Vega; Sanmi Koyejo; Vince D. Calhoun; Joshua W. Buckholtz; Juan Helen Zhou; Steffen Bollmann; Russell A. Poldrack
tags: Control and Steering; Monitoring; Trust, Delegation & Accountability
summary: Presents Brain Researcher, an agentic harness that runs neuroimaging analyses within a researcher's computational environment under rules for admissible analyses, required checks and claim scope. Reports benchmark gains in tool-selection accuracy and verifiable grounding across seven models, plus collaborator-led and self-evolving case studies using multiverse analysis and a claim-classification review step.

title: Inject, Align, Recover: Staged Post-Training for Retrieval-Free Document Knowledge Internalization
creators: Qian Kou; Xiaofeng Shi; Xiaosong Qiu; Hua Zhou
summary: Proposes IAR, a three-stage post-training framework (knowledge injection via continuation, rewrite and reconstruction objectives; answer-only QA alignment; model merging for general-ability recovery) for retrieval-free question answering over a fixed document collection. Evaluates on Common Corpus and CCI across Llama, Phi, Qwen and SmolLM families, comparing against vanilla SFT, LoRA and FAPM on domain QA accuracy and general benchmarks.

title: An Agentic Approach for Active Data Collection, Travel Behavior Modeling, and Weather-Sensitive Demand Prediction
creators: Narges Ahmadi; Yubo Jiao; Jônatas Augusto Manzolli; Jiangbo Yu; Luis Miranda-Moreno
summary: Proposes a three-agent workflow that combines a chatbot-administered, image-augmented stated-preference survey of student commuters (454 respondent-scenario observations across five weather scenarios), structured data processing, and behavioral prediction. Compares a multinomial logit model, logistic regression and random forest against nine locally deployed LLMs (2-35B parameters) under zero-shot, persona, few-shot and vision-based prompting conditions for five-class mode-choice prediction.

title: TempJail: Temporal Jailbreak Attack against Large Vision-Language Models via Subtitle Scheduling
creators: Ling Zhou; Yihao Huang; Jingling Sun; Zhiwen Tian; Yi Zeng; Qihe Liu; Shijie Zhou
summary: Proposes TempJail, a black-box jailbreak framework against large vision-language models that embeds query-aligned dialogue-style subtitles in videos and optimises their duration and timing allocation to exploit temporal processing vulnerabilities. Evaluates attack success rates on four LVLMs across two datasets against prior video jailbreak baselines.

title: From Retrieved Context to Runtime Control: Adaptive Compression for Edge-based RAG
creators: Zlatan Feric; Amir Taherin; Yanzhi Wang; David Kaeli
summary: Measures the latency and energy costs of retrieval-augmented generation with prompt-context compression on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor edge SoC, using Llama and Qwen generators, Natural Questions and HotpotQA, and LLMLingua-2. Reports that generation dominates per-query latency and GPU energy for 7B-8B models and that intermediate compression rates cut GPU energy by up to 53.2% with little quality loss, and argues for runtime telemetry-driven compression policies.

title: Enforcing LLM Safety through DMD-based Classification of Prompt-Response Embedding Dynamics
creators: Mohamed Akrout; Olivera Kotevska; Dan Wilson
summary: The paper adapts a Koopman/DMD dynamical-systems framework, previously used for hallucination detection, to black-box LLM safety classification by fitting separate predictive models for safe and unsafe regimes over prompt and response embedding trajectories and scoring new outputs via a differential residual. It evaluates the method on three safety benchmarks with three embedding models, reporting that including prompt embeddings improves detection of interaction-dependent violations.

title: MidTool: Mid-training Data Synthesis for Agentic Tool Use
creators: Fengqing Jiang; Yite Wang; Boyi Liu; Zhaoyang Wang; Canwen Xu; Zhewei Yao; Radha Poovendran; Yuxiong He
summary: The paper introduces MidTool, a pipeline for constructing an open mid-training corpus for agentic tool use by combining web, PDF and code data with supervision synthesized from real tool APIs, MCP skills and document-grounded workflows. Qwen3-4B-Base and Qwen3-8B-Base are mid-trained on the resulting mixture and then post-trained with SFT and RL, with evaluation on BFCL, tau2-Bench and MCP Universe.

title: Distilling Aggregate Mobility Statistics into a Language Model Policy for Post-Event Crowd Simulation
creators: Tatsuya Amano; Hirozumi Yamaguchi
tags: Simulation and Digital Twins; Monitoring; Partially Observable Systems
summary: The paper fine-tunes a language-model pedestrian agent policy using only aggregate mobility statistics (zone-level device counts and origin-destination flows), reweighting the model's destination distribution to a target composition via iterative proportional fitting and resampling training trajectories to correct for fine-tuning-induced class inflation. Evaluation uses mobile network counts from two baseball games, reporting a 25% reduction in destination-share error with comparable grid correlation.

title: Credit Without Ground Truth: Auditing Step-Level Credit Assignment in LLM Agents Against Executed Replay
creators: Haiyue Zhang
summary: The paper audits step-level credit assignment signals used to train LLM agents (LLM-judge scores, outcome-conditioned logprob ratios, policy confidence) against causal ground truth obtained by re-sampling alternatives and executing replay in the single-agent ALFWorld tool environment. It reports that no signal identifies causally pivotal steps better than chance, that causal contribution is sparse and its measurability model-dependent, and that in a seven-arm pre-registered training experiment apparent differences between credit rules are explained by effective training dose rather than credit content.

title: An Irreducible Quantum Advantage in Aligning World Models with Reality
creators: Josep Lumbreras; Hailan Ma; Jayne Thompson; Mile Gu
tags: Simulation and Digital Twins; Foundations & Taxonomies
summary: A theoretical paper showing that for certain classical stochastic environments, no finite-memory classical world model can preserve the optimal policy ordering or eliminate expected-reward estimation error, while a single-qutrit quantum world model reproduces the environment exactly. The result is established by explicit construction of such true worlds.

title: Truncate Bad, Upweight Good: BoN-Style Distillation via Rank-Based Classification
creators: Yarin Bar; Yaniv Romano
summary: Proposes a Best-of-N distillation objective that truncates low-ranked completions from the target support and reweights the retained upper tail, trained offline via binary cross-entropy.

summary: Builds an offline multi-agent retrieval and review system over a curated parts library for generating evidence-grounded bio-robot design reports.

summary: Surveys LLMs, knowledge bases, reasoning, and embodiment and offers a conceptual framework plus five challenges toward general embodied intelligence.

summary: Tests a quality-diversity archive of whole repository states against sequential and independent agent search in a matched compression-library experiment, finding no endpoint advantage.

creators: Poomphob Suwannapichat; Boonyarit Changaival; Caesar Wu; Pascal Bouvry
summary: Proposes RGA-Designer, a method that fine-tunes an autoregressive graph generator for LLM multi-agent communication topologies using a reward model combining task correctness and structural compactness. Reports comparable accuracy to a prior topology-design baseline with an average 20.5% reduction in token consumption.

summary: Applies PCMCI+ with bootstrap aggregation to home sleep apnea test recordings to learn dynamic causal graphs differing across sex and age subcohorts.

summary: Proposes a transformer forecasting model that partitions time series into semantic units, builds a dependency graph over them, and routes semantic blocks to experts.
